notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: On the eve of the US midterms of 3 November, oil fell 7% and WTI went below $100 after Iran's Supreme Leader was reported to have ordered the conflict resolved and Donald Trump said he was in no rush to strike, while the Revolutionary Guard seized two American drones near Qeshm Island and a tanker burned in the Strait of Hormuz. The US Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to halt California's count of 20,000 mail ballots, Trump was reported weighing pre-emptive pardons for allies, and India's voter-roll revision removed more than 90,000 names in Chamarajanagar alone. Oracle and Meta are each raising about $20 billion for AI as Anthropic reports a quarterly loss of 23 billion on revenue of 17 billion before its listing, and Russia ordered private data centres to set aside a tenth of their capacity for the state. Shop refrigeration was attacked again across Europe, hitting 17 Dutch businesses, and North Korea denied the $6.3 billion Binance theft. There was no narrative late on 2 November on France's protests, Poland's tribunal, budgets or Russia's diplomacy.
moved: The Iran thread tilted towards talks late on 2 November: Khamenei was reported to have ordered the conflict resolved, Trump said there was no rush to strike and oil fell 7%, while drones were seized near Qeshm, explosions were reported near Lengeh and a tanker caught fire in the strait.

The contested-count thread was carried on by the edition's own link and moved earlier in the electoral calendar: the Justice Department went to the Supreme Court over 20,000 California mail ballots before polls close, and India's roll deletions and Turkey's named 2028 date were added.

The AI spending thread returned after one edition without it, placed there by the Chronicle's judgment, as a build dependent on lenders and hosts: Oracle and Meta borrowing about $20 billion each, Anthropic's loss before listing, Russia's capacity order and Trump voters turning against data centres. Its 1 November reading of narrowly landing gains is withdrawn.

A thread began on hacks against shop refrigeration and exchange wallets. No expectation set by any narrative was kept or failed since the previous Chronicle; Brent below $105 on news of resumed talks stays open, as the edition reported WTI, not Brent, below $100.
silent: Russia shunned and courted, begun on 31 October, has gone three editions without a narrative and is now silent; Iran's consultation with Putin appeared only inside the Iran thread, and its sanctions expectations are still open, so this may be the sample rather than the world moving on.

Young people's protests and constitutions and courts have each gone two editions without a narrative, both of them dated 2 November; France's fourth weekend of protests falls on 7 and 8 November, so the quiet may be the gap between weekends.

Former leaders between courts and amnesty has had no narrative since 29 October, but Trump's reported pre-emptive pardons for allies appeared late on 2 November in the contested-count thread, so the subject may be running under that join.
Drones in war stays silent, though the Revolutionary Guard's seizure of two American drones near Qeshm appeared in the Iran thread late on 2 November.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, talks and the US vote
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations side by side; from 27 October to 1 November it followed the Hormuz price shock to jet fuel, mortgages, wage rounds and a Turkish fuel tax, with Brent at $117.64 on 31 October. Early on 2 November Brent fell 2% to $111 and Axios reported Netanyahu pressing for a strike after the US vote. Late on 2 November the words tilted to talks: Khamenei was reported to have ordered the conflict resolved, Trump said there was no rush to strike, oil fell 7% and WTI went below $100. The fighting did not slow: the Revolutionary Guard seized two American drones near Qeshm, explosions were reported near Lengeh and a tanker burned in the strait. The edition's case against notes the Khamenei report is a Russian paraphrase and the fire has no stated cause.
threads.direction: Since 1 November it has moved from who pays for the fuel price towards talks, with prices falling on leaders' words while incidents at sea continue.

threads.label: Brazil's election and the United States
threads.text: On 26 October Brazil's vote was read as a script in Buenos Aires, Madrid and Nairobi. On the morning of 27 October Trump called the election rigged; by that evening, after Lula's run-off win, the United States was the common party in Flávio Bolsonaro's exit, Lula's warning of persecution, about 300 US soldiers in Colombia and Machado's return to Venezuela. Its events then ran under wider joins: Flávio Bolsonaro's arrival in the United States and an amnesty plan for Jair Bolsonaro on 29 October, and Flávio's letter declaring himself president on 30 October. Nothing from Brazil has appeared since.
threads.direction: It moved from how Brazil's vote is read abroad to Washington's part in what follows, then was taken up under wider joins and fell silent.

threads.label: AI companies' listing, land and lawsuits
threads.text: On 26 October the join was an AI company listing the end of the world as a risk factor in its prospectus and the market buying the shares. Early on 27 October an edition followed data centres to county level, where land, grid and water requests were refused, and that morning Anthropic filed for a record US share listing as Elvis Presley's rights holders sued it over 200 songs. Data centres split into their own thread on 29 October. Late on 2 November Anthropic's quarterly loss before its listing and US voters turning against data centres returned in a narrative the Chronicle placed in the AI spending thread rather than reviving this one.
threads.direction: It went from the prospectus to the ground and the courts, then fell silent as its subjects were carried under the AI spending thread.

threads.label: Young people's protests and their policing
threads.text: On 26 October the join was young people in public squares; on 27 October students struck or occupied buildings in France, Mexico, India and Italy. After three silent editions the Chronicle revived it on 31 October, when protests called for the same weekend met a ban in La Rochelle and negotiation in Lisbon. On 1 November the edition carried the link forward: France deployed 70,000 security personnel for a third weekend, Toulouse diverted metro and buses, German coverage asked whether France's violence would reach its Gen Z protest, and protesters were detained in Poland. No headline reported a demand. No narrative carried it in either 2 November edition, so one more without it turns it silent; whether France deploys 50,000 or more for a fourth weekend stays open until 9 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from youth as a political image to student strikes and then to policing reported as officers counted and routes diverted, with the protesters' demands unreported.

threads.label: State housing drives and housing protests
threads.text: On the morning of 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing through states and employers with Portugal investigating police conduct at housing protests, and the part property funds play. No narrative has followed it in five editions. Mortgage rates appeared in the oil thread on 29 and 30 October, and on 31 October Lisbon's housing camps and the Rossio demonstration appeared in the protest thread.

threads.label: Public schemes passing costs to households
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. In six countries a public scheme meant to cover a cost was reported as falling short: Canadians paying for private surgery from savings and GoFundMe, German adult children billed for parents' care, Lucknow's subsidised generic pharmacies short of medicines, a Bangladeshi antivenom programme lacking funds, compensation claims from 50,000 Australians over unlawful Centrelink suspensions, and doubt over a Mexican voluntary pension scheme. The case against noted that several of these stories have run for years. No narrative has carried it since; the budgets thread begun on 2 November touches nearby ground but did not cite it.

threads.label: AI-made faces and files in checks
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated photos in the voters' register, New Zealand job seekers report being ignored as AI-written applications flood employers, an Australian court passed the first sentence under deepfake laws without jail, and fashion models face AI copies of their image. The join is that a plausible picture or document now costs little to make while checking it still takes a person's time. No narrative has carried it in the editions since.

threads.label: Broadcasts and films removed over offence
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. A Chinese platform dropped Racing-Real Madrid and La Liga broadcasts were suspended after a remark by Mbappé, an Indian court ordered a documentary on Adani and Modi taken down, a Korean drama faced calls to halt over a Gwangju episode, and Neil Young sued to stop Trump rallies using his songs. Three of the headlines were the same Mbappé story. No narrative has carried it in the editions since.

threads.label: AI spending: profit, sell-off, debt and hosts
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand beside Norwegian, Finnish and Russian disputes. On 30 October it reached US growth of 3.4% credited to AI investment; on 31 October Alphabet had its biggest fall on record, Intel lost 29% and Taiwan's state funds bought; on 1 November the falls were read as gains landing on few firms. Late on 2 November a narrative the edition did not link, placed here by the Chronicle, read the build as needing lenders and hosts: Oracle and Meta raising about $20 billion each, Anthropic reporting a quarterly loss of 23 billion on revenue of 17 billion, tech shares falling from Nasdaq to Seoul, Russia claiming a tenth of private data centre capacity, Helsinki approving principles and Trump voters turning against data centres. Its expectations on Taiwanese buying, Korean support and a 3% index fall remain open.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and local objection through a share sell-off to the build's dependence on borrowing and on the terms governments and residents set.

threads.label: Former leaders between courts and amnesty
threads.text: Begun on 29 October. South Korea's special counsel again sought, and by one report won, a death sentence for former president Yoon Suk Yeol over his martial law declaration, while in Brazil Alcolumbre planned an amnesty for Jair Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro reached the United States with Trump's consent. Spain's Zapatero, India's Azam Khan and Indonesia's anti-corruption law also appeared. No narrative has carried the court cases since; Azam Khan's release reappeared on 1 November in the constitutions thread, and late on 2 November Trump's reported pre-emptive pardons for allies appeared in the contested-count thread.

threads.label: Failed safety systems and operator blame
threads.text: Begun on 29 October and marked tentative by its own edition. A high-speed collision near Urda in Spain, which other headlines say killed 68 people, followed at least 15 warnings about faulty signalling; a JR train in Japan overran a station when its driver was drowsy and its automatic braking did not act; Bangladesh, Manila's airport and Mexico's networks had failures of grids, servers, cameras and internet. Only the Spanish and Japanese cases had a stated cause. No narrative has carried it since.

threads.label: Vote counts and rolls as contested ground
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with Flávio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil's president, Eisenkot accusing Netanyahu of delegitimising Israel's result, the Alaska inquiry, deletion forms against Muslim voters in Delhi and a disputed governorship in Imo. Early on 2 November the Chronicle placed here doubt from governing sides: Likud's black cloud over the Knesset result and Trump aides planning to govern without Congress. Late on 2 November the edition carried it on by its own link and moved it earlier: the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to halt California's count of 20,000 mail ballots, Trump was reported weighing pre-emptive pardons for allies, India's roll revision removed more than 90,000 names in Chamarajanagar, Erdogan's adviser named 16 April 2028 for Turkey's election and Netanyahu ruled out Arab parties. Its case against says Israeli coalitions have nearly always excluded Arab parties and roll revisions routinely remove the dead.
threads.direction: It has moved from contesting results after a vote to governing sides acting on ballots, rolls and pardons before the count, on the eve of the US vote.

threads.label: Drones in war, numbers and arms production
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined drones cutting power, guarding a lake, carrying the wounded and being sold. After three silent editions drones returned on 30 October, by the Chronicle's judgment, as a matter of numbers: a shortage of Ukrainian interceptors, a record raid shutting Moscow and St Petersburg airports, Finnish anti-drone training, Ukrainian loans to arms makers and Lithuanian conscription from 2032. No narrative has carried drones since; Ukrainian combat robots appeared in the AI thread on 1 November, and late on 2 November the Revolutionary Guard's seizure of two American drones near Qeshm appeared in the Iran thread.
threads.direction: It moved from the drone's many uses to the number of drones and the factories and conscripts states are raising to match them, then fell silent.

threads.label: Russia shunned by Europe, courted elsewhere
threads.text: Begun on 31 October. European ministers refused to stand beside Sergei Lavrov for the G20 photograph, while US and Russian foreign ministers discussed coordination at APEC, Washington weighed lifting sanctions on a Putin associate, Russia signed 53 documents at its Africa summit and Nigeria moved to replace a 1967 air agreement with Moscow. The case against says the Europeans still attended and the African deals renew old ties. No narrative carried it on 1 November or in either 2 November edition, so it is now silent; its expectations, a US easing of sanctions and a European objection to one, are still open. Iran's consultation with Putin appeared in the Iran thread late on 2 November.

threads.label: Constitutions and courts as political battleground
threads.text: Begun on 1 November and marked tentative by its own edition. In Poland the president and Donald Tusk's government fight over control of the Constitutional Tribunal, with protesters detained outside it; Egypt's Masrawy asks whether the constitution should be amended; a Portuguese column says Madeira should not wait for the national revision; and in India a case is filed against Mallikarjun Kharge. Its case against says only Poland's is a crisis. No narrative carried it in either 2 November edition; Israel's inquiry, India's voter-roll deletions and Turkey's 2028 election date went to the contested-count thread, which sits close to this one. One more edition without it turns it silent.

threads.label: Money leaving and states offering discounts
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined savings and fortunes moving into dollars, gold and trusts with states answering by amnesties and discounts meant to bring the money back into view. No narrative in the editions since has followed it, so it stands as a single observation. The amnesty bills of 29 October concerned convictions, not tax or hidden money.

threads.label: AI buyouts and dangerous manual work
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative set office workers being paid to leave as AI takes their tasks against labourers still dying in ditches, fields and collapsed buildings. No later narrative has carried it. On 1 November the AI thread touched nearby ground, with Micron staff payouts in Taiwan and robot guards in Jiangsu said to replace five people, but no narrative revived this join.

threads.label: Rites counted before the days of the dead
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined reports that measured the rites of late October and early November before they happen: numbers of hosts, incense sticks, costumes and the strain on worshippers' knees. No narrative has carried it since. On 31 October the only trace of Halloween was the cost of sweets inside the wage narrative, and on 1 and 2 November, All Saints' and All Souls' Days, no narrative returned to it.

threads.label: European household readiness and borrowed deterrence
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined European advice that households should be able to last 72 hours on their own with European states seeking cover from nuclear warheads they do not own. No narrative in the editions since has returned to it. Finnish anti-drone training and Lithuanian conscription on 30 October went to the drones thread, and Europe's stance towards Russia on 31 October to its own thread.

threads.label: One football night watched worldwide
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined coverage of a single football night that drew attention across many countries at once. It was tied to one event and no narrative has carried it since. Football returned on 27 October only as a broadcasting dispute in the removal-over-offence thread.

threads.label: Courts re-sentencing past events
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined courts re-sentencing events of 1979 and 1996 with a library removing material from 2026, treating them as revisions of the record. No narrative has carried it since. The former-leaders, contested-count and constitutions threads touch nearby ground, but none re-sentences an old event.

threads.label: New ways of paying and their hidden costs
threads.text: Begun early on 2 November and marked tentative by its own edition. The Hindu explains that India's no-cost EMI is a loan presented as free; Yle reports Finnish shoppers annoyed by data collection but keeping their loyalty cards; Bangladesh launches a QR code for person-to-person payments while Jawa Pos defends Indonesians who still pay cash; and the FBI blames North Korea for the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, at Binance. The join is that the visible fee has gone and the cost sits in a loan, a purchase record or an account the payer does not control. Its case against says these have different causes. Late on 2 November the Binance theft, now put at $6.3 billion and denied by North Korea, went to the new hacks thread rather than this one.

threads.label: Budgets protecting pensions over working-age incomes
threads.text: Begun early on 2 November. Italy's budget promises no pension cuts up to 25,000 euros and faster severance for civil servants. Britain's John Healey promises the benefits bill will come down, Spanish economists say a self-employed worker on sick leave can have 180 euros for the month, and Russia reminds savers how to draw pension savings. The join is that income tied to age or a salaried contract is protected while income outside it is trimmed. Its case against says Italy's is the only budget and Healey is the defence secretary. It sits near the silent public-schemes thread of 27 October, which the narrative did not cite. No narrative carried it late on 2 November.

threads.label: Hacks on shop freezers and exchange wallets
threads.text: Begun late on 2 November. Refrigeration in shops across Europe was attacked again, hitting 17 Dutch businesses while large supermarkets were unaffected; the EU called it an attack on food supply, and Finland had warned firms after attacks in France. North Korea denied stealing $6.3 billion from Binance in a twenty-minute hack whose proceeds are being laundered a second time, and a Korean brokerage and President Lee's personal details were leaked. The join is that the loss happens while the attack is under way, on equipment the smallest owners must defend. Its case against says the refrigeration attacks have no named author or gain and the Binance theft fits North Korea's pattern since 2016. The Binance theft was carried early on 2 November in the hidden-cost-of-paying thread; the Chronicle kept the two apart because this one turns on sabotage and defence.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war thread had turned to which governments carry the fuel price and which take more of it as revenue, with US-Iran talks stuck.
withdrawn.undone: On 2 November no fuel-tax argument appeared, Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well and the thread was about whether a strike or talks follow the US vote. The who-pays reading rested on Turkey's single tax rise and is not carried as the direction; its expectation of a second government raising a fuel tax is still open.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread had turned to how narrowly the gains land, on a few chip and computing makers and their staff.
withdrawn.undone: Late on 2 November the thread was about the build depending on borrowing, with Oracle and Meta raising about $20 billion each and Anthropic losing more than its revenue, and on governments and voters setting terms for data centres; no payouts were reported. The concentration reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the direction; its expectations stay open.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on ten editions over about 168 hours, with none stamped 28 October and two on 2 November about 22 hours apart, and no expectation set by any narrative has yet been kept or failed, so every direction is a reading of headlines, not a test of one. Two of today's four narratives carry continuation links; the AI narrative linked to nothing and I placed it in a live thread rather than starting a new one or reviving the silent listing thread, and the brief that asks for continuity may produce such joins as much as the world does. Today's collection was gathered hours before the US vote, so it will overweight election disputes and anything that can be tied to the vote. The Iran thread has now been read as spreading, easing, spreading, who pays, strike-or-talks and talks-with-incidents in six versions; today's tilt rests partly on a Russian paraphrase of Khamenei, and the edition's own case against says oil may have fallen on demand fears as tech shares dropped. The refrigeration attacks may look like one campaign only because English-language wires carried them to several countries. The protest, constitutions, budgets and Russia threads had nothing today, which may be the sample. My earlier versions led with the war, and I have led with it again.
line: On 2 November 2026, eve of the US midterms, oil falls 7% on reports Khamenei ordered the Iran war resolved and the Justice Department asks to halt a California count.
revision: A thread began on hacks against shop refrigeration and exchange wallets, and the AI spending thread was continued by the Chronicle's judgment, relabelled to include borrowing and hosts, with its concentration reading withdrawn. The Iran and contested-count threads were carried on by the edition's own links, Russia shunned and courted fell silent leaving eight live threads, and the standing was rewritten around oil falling on talk of talks and pre-vote moves on the US count.
